# Review Checklist: Client Windows on the Canvas

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of spec.md, plan.md, research.md and contracts/ before
`/speckit-tasks`: client robustness, input and focus, protocol scope, rendering and pacing
**Created**: 2026-11-01
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Client Robustness

- [x] CHK001 Is the "limit" for unread messages in the spec quantified, or explicitly delegated to the plan (where R8 sets 1 MiB)? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases, Plan R8]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec address an application that creates an unbounded number of objects or windows, which research R8 accepts as a known limit? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases, Plan R8]
- [x] CHK003 Is shrinking a pool through a resize request (a protocol error in contracts/protocols.md) covered by the spec's shared-memory misuse case, or only by the contract? [Consistency, Spec FR-015, Contracts protocols]
- [x] CHK004 Is "larger than RubickWay can display" defined measurably enough to test on both llvmpipe and the author's GPU (a stated limit vs "the hardware's largest image")? [Measurability, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for what the user sees or learns when RubickWay disconnects an application (log line, nothing on screen)? [Completeness, Spec FR-015, Contracts cli]
- [x] CHK006 Is the cleanup required on disconnect specified for input state held by that application: an active pointer grab, keys still held down, keyboard focus? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, Spec FR-007]
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec define what "never draws anything" means for an application that commits a buffer before its window is configured (a protocol error in the plan)? [Consistency, Spec Edge Cases, Plan R9]
- [x] CHK008 Is SC-004's "every misbehaviour listed" a closed list, so the automated test set can be judged complete? [Measurability, Spec SC-004]

## Input and Focus

- [x] CHK009 Is the behaviour of a Mod + left press on a window without keyboard focus specified (focus and raise, or canvas pan only)? [Gap, Spec FR-009, Spec FR-012]
- [x] CHK010 Is "pinch zooms the canvas even over windows" recorded in the spec, or does it exist only in the plan and contracts/input.md? [Consistency, Spec FR-013, Contracts input]
- [x] CHK011 Are right- and middle-button presses on the empty background specified (ignored, no focus change)? [Coverage, Spec FR-013]
- [x] CHK012 Is it specified whether a newly opened window takes keyboard focus while the user is in the middle of typing into, or dragging over, another window? [Edge Case, Spec FR-008]
- [x] CHK013 Is the release of a consumed compositor shortcut key specified in the spec (not delivered), or only in contracts/input.md? [Consistency, Spec FR-011, Contracts input]
- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for what applications receive when the viewer itself loses and regains keyboard focus in the host? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, Contracts input]
- [x] CHK015 Is SC-003's "within 1 logical pixel (of the window)" unambiguous about which pixel unit applies at zoom levels other than 100%? [Clarity, Spec SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 Is the cursor shown over windows specified in the spec, given that application cursor images are not shown (contracts/input.md)? [Gap, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK017 Is scrolling over a window during a pointer grab held by another window defined (goes to the grabbing window or the one under the pointer)? [Edge Case, Spec FR-010]
- [x] CHK018 Are the requirements for windows that cover each other consistent between hit-testing (topmost wins) and input regions smaller than the window (clicks fall through)? [Consistency, Spec FR-010, Data Model Windows]

## Protocol Scope

- [x] CHK019 Are application requests that the feature ignores (maximize, fullscreen, minimize, interactive move/resize from a client-drawn title bar) specified in the spec, or only in plan R9? [Gap, Spec Assumptions, Plan R9]
- [x] CHK020 Is dismissing popups immediately (plan R9) consistent with the spec's "popups are not shown yet, applications work only partially"? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK021 Is the clipboard stub (plan R10) reconciled with the spec's "no clipboard" assumption, so a reviewer can tell it is required for compatibility and transfers nothing? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, Plan R10]
- [x] CHK022 Is the list of applications the feature must work with stated as an acceptance criterion (foot and weston-terminal), rather than only as examples? [Measurability, Spec SC-001, Quickstart]
- [x] CHK023 Is the assumption that weston-terminal needs only a subset of foot's globals validated, as foot's were? [Assumption, Plan R2]
- [x] CHK024 Are the versions in plan R2 and contracts/protocols.md identical for every global? [Consistency, Plan R2, Contracts protocols]
- [x] CHK025 Is the behaviour for applications that require an unsupported global (GPU buffers) specified beyond "fail to start or fall back"? [Clarity, Spec FR-003, Spec Assumptions]

## Rendering and Pacing

- [x] CHK026 Can "smoothly (no blocky pixels, no shimmering)" in FR-005 be verified objectively, by a pixel assertion or a manual criterion? [Measurability, Spec FR-005]
- [x] CHK027 Does "visible in the viewer" in FR-006 cover partly visible windows and windows fully hidden behind other windows? [Clarity, Spec FR-006, Plan R12]
- [x] CHK028 Are requirements for translucent application content (alpha over the grid and over other windows) stated in the spec, or only in plan R5? [Gap, Spec FR-005, Plan R5]
- [x] CHK029 Is SC-002 ("within one display refresh after the terminal has drawn them") measurable with the tools named in quickstart? [Measurability, Spec SC-002, Quickstart M4]
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for a change of the viewer's display scale at runtime (the host window moved to another monitor): are applications told again? [Coverage, Spec FR-017, Plan R12]
- [x] CHK031 Does SC-005 state its assumptions about the terminals being idle (for example no blinking cursor), so the CPU target is reproducible? [Assumption, Spec SC-005]
- [x] CHK032 Is the stacking of subsurfaces relative to their window (above/below) covered by a requirement, or only by plan R5/R6? [Gap, Plan R5, Plan R6]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- Reviewed with the owner in chat on 2026-11-01: all proposed resolutions accepted; spec,
  research, data model, contracts and quickstart updated accordingly. CHK022 was answered
  with kitty (software rendering) as the acceptance application instead of foot and
  weston-terminal; CHK023 was resolved by verifying kitty's startup requirements.
